method: SHA-256 plus GNU readelf header, program-header, dynamic-section and dynamic-symbol parsing

classifier.semantics: The four categories are conservative audit labels over every unique UND dynamic symbol. They are exhaustive, but they are not provider or fallback allowlists.
classifier.default_resolution: Every unresolved name remains required according to its ELF binding and adapter contract. A category, a weak ELF binding, or an unknown name never authorizes a fabricated address or zero-return stub.
classifier.critical_unknown_policy: fail-closed; no critical or unknown name may become weak, optional, success, NULL, or no-op without a hash-pinned adapter proof and exact return/side-effect contract

common_contracts.contract: Detect ELF class, machine, float/base PCS and Android object layouts before selecting an adapter. Never pass guest FILE, stat/statfs/dirent, sigaction/sigset, pthread, condition, rwlock or semaphore storage directly to a host ABI.

Resolve every strong UND name through an exact adapter/provider or fail before guest code. Generated zero-return tables, host dlsym coincidence and symbol-name guessing are not compatibility contracts.

For each actually loaded module: map, relocate, install its ABI adapters, resolve, finalize/cache, execute all accepted constructors, initialize a stable VM/environment, then call that module's JNI_OnLoad when the native Android flow does so. Lifecycle entry points follow only afterward.

Keep JavaVM and JNIEnv identities stable across AttachCurrentThread/GetEnv and implement the exact JNI slots consumed by the guest: reference identity/lifetime, classes, method and field IDs, strings, arrays, exceptions and GetJavaVM.

RegisterNatives must key functions by class, name and signature and preserve their lifetime whenever later lifecycle dispatch consumes registered methods. Returning success without storage is allowed only for a hash-pinned adapter proving that no registered method is consumed.

The framework may enforce phase ordering, but the exact Activity, surface, resume, render, pause, save and exit calls remain adapter-owned. No engine name, Java class, game offset, callback completion or teardown skip belongs in the universal core.

global_prohibitions: No fallback based on engine family, symbol prefix, device name or firmware name may turn an unknown strong import into success, NULL or no-op.
Do not pass Android opaque objects to glibc by pointer, including FILE, stat/statfs/dirent, sigaction/sigset, pthread objects and semaphores.
Do not call JNI_OnLoad before constructors, with a temporary VM, or for a catalog module that the approved adapter does not actually load.
Do not accept a missing or invalid JNI_OnLoad version merely because Bully2, Sonic4EP2 or Horizon currently log and continue.
Do not replace RegisterNatives with success-only behavior when any registered method is later consumed.
Do not copy Rockstar, fox/f2f, Unity/IL2CPP, Aspyr or Gameloft class names, exports, offsets, callbacks, patches or exit shortcuts into the universal core.
Do not use ports/tasm2 as a positive source; only ports/asm2_127 is canonical.
